blocks.text:
**Under 28 days:** neonatal team — use the AAP 2022 phototherapy and escalation thresholds.
**Jaundice with poor feeding, lethargy, high-pitched cry, arching or abnormal tone:** possible bilirubin encephalopathy — emergency department now; also evaluate for sepsis.
**Infant with total bilirubin at or near the AAP 2022 phototherapy threshold (any cause), bilirubin:albumin molar ratio ≥ 1.0, or bilirubin rising day by day without hemolysis (think Crigler–Najjar type I):** admit for intensive phototherapy now, check bilirubin and albumin, call hepatology today.
**Pallor, dark (tea-colored) urine, rapid heart rate:** acute hemolysis — emergency department now. Hemolysis with a negative direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test, jaundice and low ALP in a sick child: think acute Wilson disease — INR now, call hepatology / transplant center now.
**Known Crigler–Najjar with fever, vomiting or fasting:** same-day bilirubin and albumin; call hepatology.
**Pale stools at any age:** same-day hepatology. **Direct bilirubin > 1.0 mg/dL (conjugated > 0.3 mg/dL) in an infant:** not unconjugated — call hepatology today; biliary atresia until proved otherwise.

items: Total and direct (or conjugated) bilirubin — non-hemolyzed sample

Direct antiglobulin test (DAT); infant: blood group of mother and infant

items: Weight trajectory and stool color — look yourself

groups.label: Only if above the Gilbert range or jaundiced since infancy

items: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia hidden by a large total — read the direct value, never the ratio
Crigler–Najjar type I — bilirubin rises ~4 mg/dL a day from birth; kernicterus in the first weeks
Hemolysis — G6PD deficiency, hereditary spherocytosis, immune hemolysis
Pigment gallstones in chronic hemolysis — right upper quadrant pain or fever
Congenital hypothyroidism in a jaundiced infant
Sepsis in a lethargic, jaundiced infant
Acute Wilson disease — Coombs-negative hemolysis with jaundice and low ALP
Low albumin or displacing drugs (ceftriaxone, sulfonamides) — free bilirubin rises while the total looks unchanged

blocks.text:
Bilirubin is handled in five steps: production from heme, transport on albumin, uptake into the liver cell, conjugation by UGT1A1, and excretion into bile. Unconjugated bilirubin rises when production goes up (hemolysis, a resorbing hematoma), when transport fails, or when conjugation is weak. Only a raised conjugated fraction points to liver or bile-duct disease (lesson 01-02).

Unconjugated bilirubin travels bound to albumin. The unbound (free) fraction crosses into the brain. Low albumin or a displacing drug raises free bilirubin while the total stays the same — so read the albumin beside the bilirubin.

Gilbert syndrome, Crigler–Najjar type II and type I are one continuum of UGT1A1 activity. In Gilbert, activity is about 30% of normal, usually from a homozygous A(TA)7TAA promoter variant (UGT1A1*28); the allele was found in 40% of healthy controls in Amsterdam (Bosma 1995). In East Asia, *6 (p.G71R) is common. Among 163 Japanese patients, bilirubin was 2.8 ± 1.1 mg/dL in typical Gilbert, 5.2 ± 2.2 in an intermediate group and 12.9 ± 5.1 in typical type II — values overlap, so there is no sharp border (Maruo 2016).

In type I, activity is absent. In 28 untreated newborns with type I, bilirubin rose 4.3 ± 1.1 mg/dL a day; 4 (14%) developed kernicterus between days 14 and 45. A total ≥ 30 mg/dL or a bilirubin:albumin molar ratio ≥ 1.0 predicted brain injury, and starting phototherapy after day 13 raised the risk 3.5-fold. About 9 hours of phototherapy a day kept children safe, but bilirubin crept up 0.46 mg/dL a year; 17 of 28 had a liver transplant (Strauss 2020). Liver transplant still cures. Gene therapy with an adeno-associated virus vector (AAV8-UGT1A1) kept 3 patients off phototherapy for at least 78 weeks in a phase 1–2 trial, but durability in a growing liver is unknown (D'Antiga 2023).

items.text: Never use the "direct > 20% of total" rule. In 79% of newborns with biliary atresia, direct bilirubin was ≤ 20% of the total (Harpavat 2011, lesson 01-02).
A hemolyzed sample lowers the measured direct bilirubin and can hide cholestasis. Redraw.
Fasting, fever, exercise or illness can double a Gilbert bilirubin. Label nothing until a repeat when the child is well and fed.
Gilbert needs no genetic test. Reassure, stop testing, and record it: UGT1A1*28/*28 calls for a lower irinotecan starting dose, and atazanavir causes visible jaundice, most in *28/*28.
The standard Gilbert test counts TA repeats. It misses *6 (p.G71R), the common variant in East Asian children — ask for sequencing.

G6PD deficiency alone or a Gilbert-type promoter alone did not raise neonatal jaundice; together they did: 31.6% with one variant allele and 50% with two, versus 9.7% with the normal promoter (Kaplan 1997).
Phenobarbital lowers bilirubin by more than 30% in Crigler–Najjar type II, not in type I (lesson 01-02). Use it only under hepatology.
In Crigler–Najjar type I, phototherapy fails in adolescence, not infancy, as the body outgrows the light (Strauss 2020). Plan transplant early.

rows.topic: When to fractionate a jaundiced infant

positions.aap_2022_hyperbili: Breastfed still jaundiced at 3–4 weeks; formula-fed at 2 weeks
positions.naspghan_espghan_2017_nc: Any infant jaundiced after 2 weeks of age

rows.note: The app fractionates any infant jaundiced after 2 weeks, breastfed or not: a missed biliary atresia costs more than one extra test.

rows.topic: What counts as abnormal direct or conjugated bilirubin
rows.note: Thresholds belong to the assay. A conjugated cut-off applied to a direct result over-refers; the reverse under-refers.

positions.bsg_2018_lft: Repeat fasting with CBC and split bilirubin; unconjugated should rise with no anemia; reassure

rows.note: No pediatric guideline. The app repeats when the child is well and fed, with CBC and reticulocytes, and does not test genes (lesson 01-02).

positions.bsg_2018_lft: Adults: unconjugated > 40 µmol/L (≈ 2.3 mg/dL) — consider rarer causes such as Crigler–Najjar and genetic testing

rows.note: No pediatric guideline; the BSG adult cut-off sits below the typical Gilbert mean (2.8 mg/dL, Maruo 2016). The app refers above 5 mg/dL when well, or jaundice since infancy — expert opinion.
